full_judgment:
2. Facts, in brief, are that the predecessor of the petitioners, as plaintiff, instituted the above suit seeking declaration that the suit land measuring 33 decimal appertaining to plot No. 122 of C. S. Khatian No. 27, Mouza Kalaia was acquired by the defendant No. 1, his cider brother, with the fund of the joint family on the averments that after the death of their father, the defendant No. 1 his elder brother, was the karjakara (karta) of the joint family and out of the joint family income the suit land was acquired by a registered kabulayat dated 26.03.1943 and thereafter homestead was constructed therein and he and the defendant No. 1, both the brothers, were living together therein but at the instance of the defendant No. 1 the record was wrongly prepared in the name of the defendant No. 1 only which clouded his title and hence the suit. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending that the suit land was acquired by the fund which he got from his father in law and also out of the income from his business and that he provided accommodation to the plaintiff in a part of the suit homestead as a mere licensee. 

 5. As it appears the High Court Division discharged the Rule holding that evidence on record shows that the plaintiff did not adduce any independent witness to prove the fact that the suit land was acquired by the fund of the joint family t and in the suit the main controversy was how the fund was provided for purchasing the suit land and since the kabala dated 26.03.1943 stands in the name of the defendant No. 1 and the khatian has also been prepared in his name, in onus was upon the plaintiff to prove his case which he totally failed.
